source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Visit the location and conduct a comprehensive accessibility inspection, making sure to cover all required areas including parking, entrances, pathways, ramps, corridors, restrooms, elevators, and more, as mandated by the relevant codes and standards such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) or local building codes.

3. Identify failed accessibility features
List each failed item separately. Specify the location (e.g., “entrance B,” “front parking lot,” “second-floor restroom”) and describe the accessibility issue in detail (e.g., “door width of 28 inches does not meet the 32-inch minimum requirement,” “ramp slope exceeds the maximum allowable 1:12 gradient,” “lack of designated accessible parking”).

4. Use standardized assessment tools
